policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV explicitly reads the plural 'his sons,' matching qere ובניו; the singular alternative is not its main wording.
ASV explicitly reads the plural 'they shall return and war,' matching ketiv ויתגרו; the singular note is classed alternative_rendering and does not decide the reading.
ASV explicitly reads 'his fortress,' matching qere מעזו rather than the ketiv's feminine suffix.
ASV's finite future wording 'his heart shall be exalted' matches ketiv ירום; the note is only an alternative rendering.
ASV explicitly reads 'shall he turn his face,' matching ketiv וישב rather than qere וישם ('set').
ASV's main wording 'whosoever acknowledgeth him' matches qere יכיר; the reversed relation in the note is classed alternative_rendering and does not decide against it.
